clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return and your move to Hollin Road, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon coming back into the family in early 1989 and your move to the rebuilt Hollin Road house that autumn, within the next five years: your late nights began, you leaned hard on Rafe at the conservatory, a wrist injury stopped your playing in the autumn of 1991, you fell into conflict with him and withdrew, your grandfather died in June 1991, and you were lost and low through 1992 with too much moving at once. Your mother filled in your college forms and you let it happen. Your father's notice mattered to you, and you were stung he had not heard of your film in 1994. The shifts in these years build slowly, each one drawing you further from your footing, and they settle as you began the exchange to Lisbon and found your drive again.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around your bonding with Joelle in early 1998 and your separation in July 1999, within the year: your insomnia began getting in the way before concerts, yet you were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions. You started with a therapist after the split, reading about families with a gambler. One shift that counts is your insomnia rising beside your highest functioning; the other is your move toward the therapist. Two shifts are enough when they belong together and mark a turn in your life, and this period is one person's own trouble, with no one else's shifts showing in those months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer diagnosis and your move away, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 and your disastrous audition in early 2002: you were running out of steam for performing and your functioning fell, you were on poor terms with your family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you bonded with Marisol that winter, moved to Fenwick with her, then split up within the year. You sank into a deep depression once you split, barely moved from the sofa at the bottom, and could not face your family. You relied gingerly on friends—Silas, Corbin, Dale, and Hamish—rather than any relative. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home. Your shifts pile up alongside hers: her illness and your burnout sit in the same months, and the trouble that followed—your depression, your distance from family, your turn toward friends—builds through 2003 and settles as you began swimming and returned to your therapist in early 2004.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your move to nursing school, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna dying in January 2008 and your move to Marlow Sound for nursing school in September 2008: you were too drained for conversation with your mother, she pressed to visit you at Alder Creek and you told her repeatedly the timing was wrong, she drove out regardless, and you kept the door shut on her. You left for nursing school and stopped speaking to your mother, a silence that held for roughly a year. Your shifts sit close together around the lodge in late July, with your mother's push and your conflict with her, and the cutoff follows within weeks of your move. This period is your own trouble with your family, with no one else's shifts showing around these months.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and your aunt Imogen's diagnosis, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and your cousin Alice's diagnosis with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, through the year that followed: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma years before, your aunt Imogen's memory began slipping and she lashes out when muddled, and your job steadied and paid well. Yet your anxiety rose—you constantly feel you ought to be driving your projects forward—and you started a sleeping pill. Around the lake weekend for Wren's mother's retirement in late October 2019: Wren was swamped with one thing after another, you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, she talks with her father and brother all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear, yet she settled once the weekend had a plan. You awoke from the small hours and could only pull back as the others rose; your sleep is at its worst around her family. Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions and the drives home were long and quiet. Your cousin Bella was diagnosed, your aunt Imogen's symptoms rose, and your functioning sank while hers rose; the two movements are one. Your shifts around her family sit in the same days in late October 2019, and they settle as you returned to regular calls with your mother.
